## Requirements (from the contract)

1. `policy/src/policy/transparency.py` — S-1…S-14 as code (J3 §9.1 verbatim),
   one module / one vocabulary (J3 T-6); a second scrub implementation is a
   defect. The J3 §3.5 never-exported list is enforced at the emit layer
   (`explicit_columns` refuses a named member — a never-exported field reaching
   emit is a defect, not data).
2. Fail-closed secret gate (SIG-TRANSP-022) — `find_secrets` is the one shared
   detector; `ops.publish.assert_publish_set_secret_free` runs it over EVERY
   file in the publish set (site tree, staged release tree, export tree)
   before the release record is written and before any remote sync; one hit
   aborts in dry-run AND `--apply`; the refusal names file + pattern class,
   never the value; no override flag.
3. Capture-tier derivation (NEW-2 / F-400) — the writer's constant `'public'`
   is gone: `storage_tier` derives from the source's redistribution lane +
   Part VIII class (`raw-ok`+P8-clear → `public`; `derived-only`/`link-only`
   → `restricted`; `restricted` lane or P8-1/P8-2/P8-4 or any unknown →
   `sealed`). Existing rows keep their recorded tier (append-only, no
   backfill); the API's served value is the recorded tier floored by the lane
   at read time, and any tightening is labelled (`tier_basis` +
   `recorded_tier`), never a silent `public` upgrade.
4. `/v1/evidence` reads the recorded tier — `source_uri` only for `public`
   tier captures; `bytes_available` honest (P34.25 preserved); `retrieved_at`
   is full ISO-8601 UTC, never date-only (J4 S-10 / J1).
5. Tests: one planted violation per S-rule; a planted secret per detector
   pattern aborts a fixture publish; the lane×class matrix holds (unknown →
   `sealed`, never `public`); the never-exported list asserted absent.
6. Requirement stamps in the PR body: **SIG-TRANSP-022** (owner),
   **SIG-TRANSP-020** (also), **F-400** (owned finding), **J3 T-6**, **D-J3-1**,
   **P32.2**/**P34.25** (the surfaces this corrects).
